name: Operator acceptance gate and runtime-faithful verification
objective: Put the product owner back in the loop: record how the operator runs and views the product as durable truth and require real-browser verification in that runtime (and prod when it differs); make every operator-visible phase stop pending with a concrete walkthrough before its review can pass, with operator-reported failures becoming fix slices; add a 'works as a product' dimension (every control does something, interaction states, liveness over time, dev+prod) and a fresh-eyes UX walkthrough beside record fidelity; route operator-question catalogues into the gate or deferred jobs so no review passes with unrouted questions; seed a terse cumulative product smoke list re-run by each phase; require the review executor to spot-check the running product itself; ship as the next workspace version with the installer rebuilt and adopters able to pick it up via update.

review.note: F1-F6 shipped as intent.md states; engine, seeds, prose, executor prompts and v32 release validated together incl. the operator-failure cycle; docs consolidated (architecture v0005, operations v0027, qa v0003, decisions v0035). Legacy-shaped phase (no acceptance block) — reviewed under the legacy path.
